column3: Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says “the land”; BSB specifies Judah.
The Hebrew initially leaves the king of Egypt unnamed and uses pronouns for the brothers; BSB initially names Neco and explicitly identifies the brothers.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says “him”; BSB names Jehoiakim.
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says eight years old; BSB says eighteen.
The Hebrew says “at the return of the year” and “his brother”; BSB says “In the spring” and identifies Zedekiah as a relative of Jehoiachin.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says “from the mouth of the LORD”; BSB expresses this as speaking for the LORD.
The Hebrew leaves the subject unnamed here; BSB names Zedekiah.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew uses the image of rising early and sending; BSB expresses this as “Again and again.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew leaves the final giver and recipient unnamed; BSB names God and Nebuchadnezzar.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew leaves the plural subject unnamed; BSB names the Chaldeans.
The Hebrew uses an active singular without naming the subject; BSB uses the passive and names Nebuchadnezzar.
The Hebrew begins with fulfilling the word of the LORD; BSB moves that purpose to the end.
The Hebrew says “by the mouth of Jeremiah”; BSB says “spoken through Jeremiah.” It narrates the proclamation as a separate action; BSB connects it with “to send.”
Close to the Hebrew.
